name: Saint-Nazaire
title: Saint-Nazaire Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships
description: UTM and thickness measurement in Saint-Nazaire and the Loire estuary: LNG carriers at Montoir, tankers at Donges, hull structure and pre-docking gauging.
h1: Thickness Measurement and Hull Inspection in Saint-Nazaire
intro: Saint-Nazaire is best known for building large cruise ships, but the gauging work in the Loire estuary comes from the ships that trade there: LNG carriers at the Montoir terminal, tankers at the Donges refinery jetties, bulk, container and ro-ro ships at Montoir, and the service vessels of the offshore wind farm. Superintendents call us to measure hull structure and tanks during a call, ahead of a docking elsewhere, or for an owner's newbuilding team. We mobilise a team from India to the estuary for each call.

highlights.p: LNG carriers at Montoir and tankers at Donges are gauged within the terminals' safety rules, usually in empty ballast tanks on a laden arrival and on deck where electronic instruments are permitted.
Saint-Nazaire is a shipbuilding port, not a commercial repair port. Ships calling in the estuary are gauged afloat so the steel list for a docking at Brest or further afield is ready in advance.
At the cruise newbuilding yard, an owner's site team can commission independent UT of welds or thickness checks on owner-furnished items, arranged through the owner and the yard.

port.h: Saint-Nazaire and the Loire estuary port
p: Saint-Nazaire stands at the mouth of the Loire and is the seaward part of Nantes Saint-Nazaire Port, whose terminals line the estuary from Saint-Nazaire through Montoir-de-Bretagne and Donges up to Nantes. The town is defined by Chantiers de l'Atlantique, the shipyard that builds some of the largest cruise ships afloat as well as offshore wind substations and naval auxiliaries. Its building docks, outfitting quays and the steel and outfitting subcontractors around them make the estuary one of Europe's main shipbuilding centres.

The cargo port is energy-led. The Montoir LNG terminal receives LNG carriers, the TotalEnergies refinery at Donges is served by crude and product tankers at its jetties, and the Montoir terminals handle containers, ro-ro cargo, agricultural bulk and other dry cargo. The Saint-Nazaire offshore wind farm off the estuary mouth has added crew transfer and service vessels to the local fleet. Further upriver, Nantes handles smaller cargo ships and river-sea traffic, so the estuary carries everything from deep-draught LNG carriers to coasters within a single port authority.

For gauging, the important point is that Saint-Nazaire is not a commercial ship-repair port in the way Brest or Dunkirk are. A ship that needs a docking survey normally goes to a repair yard elsewhere, and Brest is the nearest port with large commercial dry docks, so in-service gauging here is done afloat: at the LNG and oil jetties within their safety rules, at the Montoir cargo berths, in the locked basins at Saint-Nazaire, or while a ship lies at anchor off the estuary. Deep-draught ships work to tidal windows in the Loire channel, and the waiting time those windows create can be used for ballast-tank and deck gauging. The newbuilding yard creates a different kind of demand: an owner's site team may want independent UT of welds or thickness checks on owner-furnished items before delivery, alongside the yard's own quality control.

facilities.h: Gauging locations along the Loire estuary
p: The LNG terminal at Montoir-de-Bretagne and the refinery jetties at Donges are the two energy berths. LNG carrier thickness measurement here is limited to what the terminal's gas-safety rules and the ship's permit-to-work allow during cargo operations, which usually means ballast tanks, empty on a laden arrival, and the weather deck where the terminal permits electronic instruments. Thickness gauging at Donges follows the same logic on crude and product tankers: ballast tanks and deck structure at the jetty, with cargo-tank work kept for a gas-free yard stay after the ship leaves the estuary.

The Montoir cargo terminals and the Saint-Nazaire basins, entered through locks, give longer and simpler windows for dry-cargo ships. Container ships, ro-ro ships and bulk carriers can be gauged in holds, ballast tanks and on deck during their stay, and ships laid by in the basins suit pre-purchase or condition surveys. For an owner's newbuilding team at the shipyard, any independent UT of welds or thickness checks on owner-furnished items is arranged through the owner and the yard, and the yard's quality control and the class newbuilding survey remain the acceptance route.
list: Montoir LNG terminal — ballast-tank and deck gauging on LNG carriers within the terminal's gas-safety rules, usually on a laden arrival with ballast tanks empty.
Donges refinery jetties — ballast-tank and deck structure gauging on crude and product tankers, with cargo tanks left for a gas-free yard stay.
Montoir container, ro-ro and dry-bulk terminals — hold, hatch coaming, ballast-tank and deck gauging on cargo ships during their call.
Saint-Nazaire wet basins behind the locks — ships laid by between employment, suited to pre-purchase, on-hire or condition gauging worked over consecutive days.
Estuary anchorage off Saint-Nazaire — launch-served ballast-tank gauging on deep-draught ships waiting for a berth or for the tide.
Nantes upriver berths — gauging on smaller cargo and river-sea ships, reached by road on the same mobilisation.
The cruise newbuilding yard, for owners' site teams — independent weld UT or thickness spot checks on owner-furnished items, arranged through the owner and the yard.

context.h: Regulation and market context on the Loire
p: Saint-Nazaire is outside every SOx ECA in force today: the Bay of Biscay lies well south of the North Sea ECA's 48°30'N limit. IMO's decision at MEPC 84 in 2026 to create a North-East Atlantic ECA ends that: the amendment enters into force on 1 September 2027, and the 0.10% sulphur limit reaches the French Atlantic coast in September 2028. Product tankers and short-sea ro-ro ships trading regularly into the Loire will then burn ECA fuel or run scrubbers in ECA mode all the way in, and owners planning dockings over the next two years can add scrubber piping gauging to the scope now.

Ships calling on the Loire are inspected under the Paris MoU regime, and each call counts towards the owner's EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime obligations, in force since 2024 and 2025 respectively. For in-service tankers at Donges the ESP framework applies, with IACS UR Z10.4 for double-hull oil tankers, and charterers and oil-major vetting often ask for CAP on tankers over about 15 years; a product tanker on regular Donges service is a typical case for planning that gauging into its next docking. LNG carriers calling at Montoir are not ESP ships and are gauged under UR Z7 and their society's gas carrier rules, with the inner hull of membrane ships measured from the ballast side.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Saint-Nazaire
jobs.p: Jobs on the Loire are short and berth-driven, with the tide and the terminals setting the windows, and the docking itself usually happens at a yard outside the estuary. We plan around the berth line-up and the ship's tidal transit, and take first the readings the superintendent needs for the next docking or survey, leaving the rest for the yard. Requests for UTM in the Loire estuary typically include:
list: Ballast-tank gauging on a membrane LNG carrier on a laden arrival at Montoir, giving the superintendent inner-hull and double-bottom readings ahead of its intermediate docking.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks and deck structure on a product tanker at the Donges jetties, before it sails for a renewal survey at a yard elsewhere.
Gauging of hatch covers, coamings and hold frames on a bulk carrier at the Montoir dry-bulk terminal, documenting steel condition as it delivers into a new charter.
Pre-purchase gauging on a short-sea cargo ship laid by in the Saint-Nazaire basins, completed while the buyer's inspector reviews records and machinery.
Independent UT of welds and plate thickness spot checks on owner-furnished items for an owner's site team before delivery of a newbuilding.
Baseline wall-thickness readings on the scrubber wash-water and overboard lines of a short-sea ro-ro ship, so worn spools are replaced before 2028 brings the Atlantic ECA.

logistics: Nantes Atlantique Airport is the closest international airport, and Paris Charles de Gaulle with a high-speed train towards Nantes and Saint-Nazaire is the alternative when connections from India suit it better. The ship's agent arranges ISPS passes for the LNG and oil terminals, which have their own induction and safety requirements, and launch boats for ships at the estuary anchorage. Each technician needs a Schengen visa, applied for in India once the call or docking date is firm, with an invitation letter from the owner or agent. Tidal windows can shift berthing times, so boarding is confirmed with the agent on the day.

faqs.q: Is there a repair dry dock at Saint-Nazaire for a docking survey?
faqs.a: Saint-Nazaire is a shipbuilding port rather than a commercial repair port, so ships that need a docking survey normally go to a repair yard elsewhere; Brest is the nearest port with large commercial dry docks. What we offer at Saint-Nazaire is the gauging before that docking: ballast tanks, holds and deck structure measured during the call so the yard specification carries real steel figures.

faqs.q: Can you gauge an LNG carrier at the Montoir terminal?
faqs.a: Within the terminal's rules, yes. On a laden arrival the ballast tanks are empty, which is the right time to gauge the double bottom, side tanks and the inner hull from the ballast side. Work on deck in hazardous zones needs the terminal's and the ship's permission for electronic instruments, and anything the terminal will not allow during cargo operations is left for the next docking.

faqs.q: Do you also cover Donges and the Nantes berths upriver?
faqs.a: Yes. Donges, Montoir, Saint-Nazaire and Nantes are all part of the same estuary port and reached by road, so one mobilisation can cover a tanker at the Donges jetties and a cargo ship at Nantes if the berth times allow. Ship inspection in Nantes is usually on smaller cargo and river-sea ships, where holds, ballast tanks and hatch covers are the main items.

faqs.q: Will the North-East Atlantic ECA affect ships calling at the Loire?
faqs.a: Yes, from 2028. The Loire is outside every ECA in force today, but the North-East Atlantic ECA adopted at MEPC 84 brings France's Atlantic waters in, with the 0.10% sulphur limit applying from September 2028. Scrubber-fitted ships will then run in ECA mode on approach, so dockings planned before then are a sensible time to gauge wash-water and overboard piping and set a baseline.
